film: SC-158 · the Mango Drink demo film
opening: Near-expiry stock, routed by AI agents. One yes from a person.

lines.text: Munchly Foods makes it. By the time a batch reaches a distributor's godown, the clock on its best-before is already running.
Lakshmi Agencies holds 2,000 packs of Mango Drink 200 ml, batch MF-2410-118, with 22 days to best-before.
Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart stop taking a pack this close to its date: three gates, all crossed. Destroying it would cost ₹23,059.
Smart-Clearance is software as a service: Munchly's workspace is one of many, set up and watched by the platform's staff in the console.
Every client's batches in flight, the agents at work on each stop, what was recovered, and the food kept out of landfill, day by day.
Ten agents on Gemini work a batch: Watcher, Vision, Valuer, Router, Lister, Negotiator, Outreach, Donation, Paperwork and Impact. A person says yes once.
Each client's own rules: the quick-commerce gates, the exits and their prices, the kirana scheme, the expiry policy.
Every morning the Watcher checks every batch at every distributor against sell-through and the gates.
1,608 packs will not sell before 24 Oct. Priya is told on her phone, in the words she reads.
The batch has its own page: flagged, at risk, and what each agent does next. Nothing is hidden from the operator.
One photo of the carton's label is all Vision asks of the distributor. Bas ek photo.
Her Today card asks for it: take a photo, or upload one.
Vision reads the batch, MFG, best-before and MRP from the label and matches them to the DMS export. The batch is real, and it is this one.
The Valuer prices five exits. The Router splits the batch: 1,372 to the kiranas, 150 to the staff sale, 86 to Feeding India. Net ₹16,888, ₹22,258 better than the bin.
Priya says yes once, from her phone. The approval is logged with who, when and device.
The distributor is told the plan, with a Pause. The agents set off: Outreach to the shops, Donation to the food bank, the staff sale opened.
58 shops in the old city get the offer in their own language: buy 10, get 2 free, for 48 hours.
In her app: the scheme, her cap (what she sells in two weeks, times four) and her margin. She orders in a tap.
₹20 MRP packs at ₹12 effective: with 2 free in every 12, ₹8 a pack stays with the shop. Fresh stock at a scheme price, with no haggling.
A fair price for the shop, a fair price for the customer, and a brand that keeps its shelf.
52 shops order 1,372 packets inside the window, each under its cap. Every order is a line in the audit trail.
150 packs for the godown's own staff at ₹8, paid on UPI at the gate, recorded once by the distributor.
Recorded: 150 of 150 sold. What sold is what counts; nothing is assumed.
Packs with 15 or more days left go to a food bank, with the FSSAI surplus-food checklist drafted for them.
Feeding India collects 86 packs at the godown: 86 meals served, instead of 86 packs in a landfill.
Feeding India issues its own donation receipt, numbered in its own series, with its PDF. Munchly and the distributor each keep a copy.
The Saturday round delivers the scheme to every shop that ordered.
Her deliveries, batch by batch: the round to the shops, the staff sale, the food bank's pickup.
Paperwork drafts the pack and lays each paper out as a PDF: the credit note, the GST memo, the FSSAI checklist, the receipt.
The credit note: Munchly's price support to Lakshmi Agencies, so the distributor ends whole on the batch. A financial note, with no GST adjustment.
The GST memo: input credit kept on every pack sold, reversed only on the 86 given away. ₹837 of credit stays with Munchly.
The FSSAI checklist for the donation, drafted from the batch's own dates and the food bank's rules.
On expiry day nothing is left at the godown. Impact posts the ledger, and the batch is cleared.
₹16,888 recovered on a batch that was headed for a ₹23,059 write-off.
One ledger, three readings. Money: what was recovered against the would-be write-off, every batch a segment, by quarter and by year.
GST: input credit kept and reversed under s.17(5)(h), the invoices and the credit notes, exported as the CA receives them.
Impact: 346 kg of food kept out of landfill, 864 kg of CO₂e avoided, 86 meals, and BRSR Principle 6's food-waste row with its evidence.
The batch's own BRSR line and its evidence: 52 kirana order logs, CN/0117, the FSSAI checklist, receipt FI/HYD/26-27/0417.
And in the console, across every client: food kept out of landfill by day, and what was destroyed, on one scale.
The brand recovers. The distributor ends whole. The kiranas earn. The food bank serves.
